- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.50), model tends to overcorrect upward; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; cap forecast at 1–2 days above peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive (0.00), model underestimates volatility; increase forecast slope slightly to reflect higher-than-average movement.
- Model consistently underestimates true price peaks in 30-day horizon; add 2–5% buffer to forecasted maxima if recent history shows upward momentum.
- If sentiment is positive and price is rising, model may lag; adjust forecast to align with 1–2 day lag in true price trend.
- When sentiment is positive and price is flat or declining, model often overestimates future rise; reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline after peak), model tends to ignore it; apply downward bias of 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
